# Monthly IC Memo — 2026-11

Session SESSION_MONTHLY_IC · 2026-11-07 · Aldrich (JUDGE), for the IC
Scope: third monthly IC. Packet performance figures are inception-to-date (fund start 2026-07-11, n=90 observations) unless labelled "month" (window since the 2026-10-03 IC).

sections.heading: Posture
sections.markdown:
The fund is deployed for the first time. INDO carries **3 names, 14.4% gross, 85.6% cash**; GLOBAL remains **0 names, 100% cash**. Governor **NONE** in both books. Max drawdown **−0.07% (GLOBAL) / −1.71% (INDO)** — both far inside the −8% REVIEW threshold, so the governor machinery has still never been exercised. Four INDO buys were filled this month (ERAA and MEDC on 10-16, a MEDC add on 10-20, PTBA on 11-06); no GLOBAL fill.

The compliance block is unchanged in kind: cash above the 40% ceiling in both books, and GLOBAL still below the 60–95% deployment band. INDO's 14.4% is a first step, not a ramp.

sections.heading: Attribution — what worked and what didn't
sections.markdown:
INDO contribution since inception (packet attribution):

| Name | Contribution (IDR) | Since-entry move |
|---|---|---|
| PTBA.JK | **+10,976,172** | +1.71% |
| ERAA.JK | **−45,031,980** | −6.29% |
| MEDC.JK | **−62,464,631** | −6.97% |

Net position contribution is **−96.5m IDR**; the book's positive return comes from cash carry, not from the equity sleeve. Sector exposure: CONSUMER 4.32% NAV, ENERGY 5.38%, COAL 4.72%. Factor exposure: energy 10.1% NAV, oil_gas 5.38%, coal_china 4.72%, domestic_cycle 4.32%, digital_id 4.32% (factors overlap; a name can carry more than one).

**Worked:** PTBA is the only positive contributor. It is also the only one of the three whose entry was struck at the market (limit 3,000 against a 2,950 close); the two losers were filled on limits roughly 14–15% below spot, i.e. only after the market had fallen to them.

**Didn't:** ERAA and MEDC are both down 6–7% since entry, and both fell further after the fill. ERAA is the macro transmission case the desk itself named — an import-heavy retailer exposed to IDR funding cost on both COGS and discount rate — and it has behaved as the transmission note predicted. MEDC carries the oil-and-gas exposure into a week in which Brent fell 13%; it is the larger absolute loss despite a smaller percentage move, on a bigger position. Neither is near its kill level (ERAA 17.1% above, MEDC 30.4% above), so no exit is due. The open question for next month is not the theses — both are behaving as written — but the fill discipline: buying 14–15% below spot in a falling tape is how a correct thesis still loses money early.

sections.heading: Kill ledger
sections.markdown:
**43 kills inception-to-date, all with a post-kill print.** **23 avoided further loss, 18 left gains on the table, 2 are flat**; the average kill now trades **−1.2%** below its kill price, i.e. the kill discipline is marginally value-adding in aggregate. Reason mix: other 19, valuation 15, process 6, liquidity 1, fragile_estimates 1, base_rate 1.

**Month window (15 kills):** average **+1.97%** above the kill price — the month's kills were, on average, slightly early. 7 avoided loss, 7 missed gain, 1 flat. Reason mix: other 10, valuation 5.

| Worst misses | Killed | Reason | vs kill |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASII.JK | 10-19 | valuation | **+22.5%** |
| KLBF.JK | 10-19 | other | **+19.8%** |
| JSMR.JK | 10-03 | other | +9.1% |
| SAP | 10-12 | other | +8.7% |

| Best avoids | Killed | Reason | vs kill |
|---|---|---|---|
| DMAS.JK | 10-12 | other | **−12.0%** |
| BAC | 10-03 | other | −8.1% |
| SMFG | 10-19 | valuation | −5.8% |

Two structural observations, both evidence-only:

1. **The two worst misses are both re-kills at a lower price.** ASII was first killed 07-22 at 5,150 and re-killed 10-19 at 4,080; KLBF was first killed 09-02 at 755 and re-killed 10-19 at 630. Both then rebounded to roughly the first kill's price. The re-test was performed (both were deep-dived on fresh FY2025/H1-26 prints), but in both cases the rebuilt target was cut alongside the entry, so the name still failed the hurdle at a price 20% below where it had already been rejected. TOWR, the third re-kill of that session, is the counter-example: it kept falling (−3.3%), so the pattern is not "re-kills are always wrong" — it is that a re-kill whose only new fact is a lower price needs its target held to valuation, not re-based to the new price.
2. **The "other" tag is mostly a recording artifact, not a verdict pattern.** "other" is 44% of the ledger and two-thirds of this month's kills, but on inspection 14 of the 19 "other" rows name a real reason in the verdict text. The ledger writer only accepts a literal `reason_tag: ` drawn from a seven-value list, so a verdict that writes the tag with a backtick instead of a colon (BAC), a reason outside the list (`no_variant_perception`, SAP), or a prose-only verdict (KLBF) all collapse to "other". The month's second-worst miss (KLBF) is one of these. The fix belongs in the ledger writer, not in the Judge's behaviour — but until it is fixed the reason mix cannot be used to score verdict quality.

sections.heading: Sizing-deviation review
sections.markdown:
**Zero discretionary deviations.** Every size this month was the script anchor times the Judge multiplier, applied unsoftened: ERAA 10.0 × 0.5 = 5.0% NAV, MEDC 10.0 × 0.6 = 6.0%, PTBA 10.0 × 0.5 = 5.0%, JPFA 10.0 × 0.5 = 5.0%. The PM never cut below the mechanical product and never raised above it. The script→PM deviation lane therefore remains unexercised in the loss-making direction — there is no evidence yet on whether PM discretion adds or destroys value.

One sizing note with investment content: the V5.4 carry ruling (dividend carry earned on the up leg only) re-sized AADI and TINS to zero and 0.09% respectively, clearing their previously recorded sizes. Both now sit awaiting PM sizing. That ruling is doing real work — it removed two positions that the old convention had credited with carry in their own failure state.

sections.heading: Hurdle ruling
sections.markdown: The desk has been carrying two different equity hurdles: an informal "cash proxy + ~4%" (~9.5%/yr) in triage and cards, and the house card's "5–10y FR net carry + ~4%/yr" (10.44%/yr on the 10y print theses use — 7.16% gross, 6.44% net of the 10% coupon tax, plus 4). **The card governs.** The alternative to a multi-year equity position is a multi-year sovereign, not overnight cash, so the hurdle is duration-matched: the 5–10y FR net carry plus ~4%/yr, read from the current curve at every judgment. The lower number is deprecated. Under the governing hurdle, several previously judged passes clear by well under a percentage point rather than decisively, and none of them is a live position, so no trade is invalidated today. This ruling is a clarification of the existing card, not a new law. It also has a retroactive reading: the three 10-19 re-kill chains were judged against the gross 11.2%/yr. On the correct 10.44%, ASII (8.9%/yr) and KLBF (3.0%/yr) still fail, while TOWR's stated legs (+36.3% over 3 years, ~10.85%/yr) would clear — its kill survives on the gap-adjusted downside (−43% fill, not the stated −35%), not on the hurdle. All three verdicts stand, but two of them were reached on the wrong ruler.

sections.heading: Governor episodes
sections.markdown: None. Governor NONE in both books for the whole record; no REVIEW, no DEGROSS, no de-gross tickets, no recovery memo. The exit-to-flat machinery is untested, not proven.

sections.heading: Coverage
sections.markdown:
**85 of 975 names published (8.7%)**, 4 in progress (2 in red-team, 2 in draft), 134 parked, **0 stale**, 2 NOT RATED. Rating distribution: BUY 27, ADD 5, HOLD 16, REDUCE 12, SELL 23, NOT RATED 2 — 32 positive against 35 negative, a balanced book rather than a promotional one.

The rollout is where it should be: the pilot industries are effectively complete (COAL 21/26, COAL_LOGISTICS 15/21, CONGLOMERATES 10/12), and the remaining desks are early (ENERGY 37/78 overall; BASIC_MATERIALS 14/116; INDUSTRIALS 10/75; CONSUMER_NON_CYCLICALS 7/135; CONSUMER_CYCLICALS 6/168; FINANCIALS 9/106; TECHNOLOGY 1/47; INFRASTRUCTURES 1/67; HEALTHCARE 0/41; PROPERTIES 0/96; TRANSPORTATION 0/44). Every industry has been open since 2026-11-05, so the queue is now ordered by fund-universe membership and market cap rather than by pilot scope.

Driver validation is clean on errors (0 across all six decks) with three coal warnings outstanding — ICI-3 and the two royalty tables still need sourced values. Deck drift is within review: all ten tracked variables are marked reviewed, with the largest gaps between spot and FY2027E at tin +45.2%, ICP +44.6%, Newcastle +27.4% and copper +25.5% on the high side, and wheat −26.1%, silver −20.1% and corn −18.9% on the low side. No deck has blocked an industry for more than two weeks; all nine deck queue items are closed.

sections.heading: Next-month posture
sections.markdown:
1. **Deployment, not analysis, is the binding constraint.** INDO is at 14.4% against a 60–95% band and GLOBAL at 0%. The pipeline is producing judged theses (3 live, 6 judged-unticketed, 3 awaiting PM sizing) but the entry levels sit far below spot by design. The honest question for December is whether the value levels are right or whether the sourcing is producing names whose value is structurally below market.
2. **The re-kill lane now has a rule.** Two of this month's three re-kills missed 20%+ because the target was re-based down with the price. This session's consolidation added a Judge rule: on a re-kill at a materially lower price, a sub-hurdle result is a price objection, not a thesis failure, unless a stated KPI has fired or a printed number impairs earnings quality. TOWR and SMFG are the bounding cases where the kill earned.
3. **Fix the kill-reason record before scoring verdict quality.** The "other" tag is a parser artifact (see above), so the reason mix currently understates how tightly verdicts are typed. Repair the ledger writer, then re-score the mix.
4. **Calibration is still the gap.** Calibration n=0 for a third consecutive month: no judged thesis has reached a closed P&L with a recorded outcome, so Judge/Bear calibration, per-sleeve and per-archetype hit rates remain unmeasured. The kill ledger is still the only realised signal, and it scores kills, not passes. The first closed position will be the first real calibration datum — ERAA, MEDC and PTBA are the candidates.
5. **Keep the teeth that work:** base-rate kills (QCOM −8.5%), the liquidity veto, the fragile-estimates gate, and the V5.4 carry ruling.
6. Fees verification current (last verified 2026-07-06, 12-month cycle, not due). No action.
